verdict.rationale: Requesty documents service accounts as non-human identities whose key spend is not tied to a user, and each API key or service account can have its own monthly spend cap, so an agent can get its own budget-capped key. The pack has no evidence of per-key rate limits: the rate-limit mention is about provider failures triggering fallback, and the Guardrails feature is content scanning, not a rate control. missing for 10: per-key rate/request-throughput limits, details on cap enforcement behavior (hard stop vs alert), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can give an autonomous agent its own key with budget and rate guardrails so it cannot run away on spend

citations.quote: Each API key or service account can have its own monthly spend cap.
Service accounts allow you create non-human entities... spend from those keys will not be tied to any user.
